title: Floating Machi Koro-style central illustration spec
purpose: Reusable specification for the central subject illustration that will be composited onto a blank Machi Koro-style card furniture template.

integration_context.target_use: Generate only the central content illustration to be pasted onto an existing blank card template.
integration_context.background_requirement: Genuinely transparent background. No sky, header, footer, card furniture, text, coin, icon, frame, or backdrop.
integration_context.text_policy: The illustration must contain absolutely no letters, numbers, words, prices, menus, labels, signs, logos, graffiti, license-plate characters, or text-like pseudo-glyphs on any surface.
integration_context.card_relationship: The art should sit like a floating miniature object or sticker inside the middle of the card, leaving generous transparent space around it.
integration_context.central_positioning: The subject should be centered, self-contained, fully visible, and surrounded by ample transparent margin.

style_goal.primary_rule: Match the cute simplified establishment-art language of the original Machi Koro tabletop game without copying a specific illustration.
style_goal.secondary_rule: Depict a culturally recognizable 1990s beer kiosk from central Russia without making the rendering realistic.
style_goal.core_formula: Cute simplified board-game miniature plus a bleak, familiar post-Soviet roadside beer kiosk.

what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.miniature_scene_feel: A small isolated toy-like scene, like a board-game token or floating diorama, not a full landscape.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.shape_language: Large clean shapes, simple geometry, compact clustered forms, and a crisp readable silhouette.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.perspective: Loose playful three-quarter perspective, facing slightly right and showing the front and right side.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.linework: Clear outlines or sharp separations between forms, with sparse interior detail.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.shading: Simple graphic shading using one or two darker tones, never realistic lighting.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.materials: Painted sheet metal, glass, concrete, and asphalt communicated mostly by color and silhouette, not texture.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.detail_density: Low to moderate and readable at small card size.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.silhouette_priority: The narrow old kiosk, faceted corners, glass display bays, low service hatch, and bowed sheet-metal awning must read instantly.
what_machi_koro_art_looks_like.scene_boundary: The kiosk rests on a small stylized pavement slab and does not blend into any background.

visual_composition.occupancy: Compact horizontal subject intended to occupy about 30-45% of card height after compositing.
visual_composition.shape: One narrow, slightly tall kiosk with clipped corners, a raised boxy roof crown, glass display bays, and a broad bowed two-panel metal awning.
visual_composition.floating_behavior: The miniature floats in transparent space and never connects to the card skyline.
visual_composition.base: A small irregular cracked-asphalt and concrete slab belonging entirely to the miniature.
visual_composition.background: None; transparent pixels outside the miniature.

russian_grimness_rules.principle: Russian grimness comes from the utilitarian kiosk and restrained wear, not realistic rendering.
use: old monochrome gray painted sheet metal
chipped paint, dull oxidized panels, and restrained reddish-brown rust seams
raised boxy roof crown and low service hatch
broad bowed two-panel sheet-metal awning on thin supports
misted display glass with rows of plain amber beer bottles
russian_grimness_rules.guardrail: Preserve the cute board-game miniature rendering and express 1990s central-Russian specificity through object choice, palette, and a few iconic details.

warm_accents: rows of amber beer bottles behind glass
a dim amber glow inside the serving hatch
palette.saturation: low and nearly monochrome except for the amber beer
palette.overall_brightness: old, subdued, and shabby but still cute and readable

general: Reduce the kiosk to a compact iconic miniature.
Choose only the few details needed for recognition.
Show the kiosk facing slightly right, with its front and right side visible.
building_specific: Use the supplied photo as the architectural and weathering reference: a narrow old gray prefab kiosk with clipped corners, framed display windows, and a raised boxy roof crown.
Place a small low serving hatch beneath a broad bowed two-panel sheet-metal awning supported by thin diagonal rods.
Fill the front and right-side display bays with simplified rows of identical plain amber and brown beer bottles and a few aluminum beer cans, all completely unlabeled.
Show age through broad chipped-paint patches, oxidized edges, dull gray streaks, mossy lower stains, and a few restrained rust seams rather than realistic texture noise.
Keep every fascia, wall panel, shutter, window, hatch, bottle, crate, and surface completely free of lettering, numbers, logos, labels, and pseudo-writing.
Avoid blank signboards, menu boards, price boards, posters, banners, and product displays.
environment_specific: Use a tiny self-contained cracked-asphalt and concrete base.
Keep the beer inside the glass display bays; optionally place one small plain metal keg beside the kiosk, with no loose crate or bin.
Do not include people, vehicles, streets, trees, apartment blocks, or surrounding buildings.

content.subject: A classic 1990s beer kiosk from a small town in central Russia.
content.description: A narrow, slightly tall gray prefab kiosk matching the supplied photo: clipped corners, framed display windows, a raised boxy roof crown, a broad bowed two-panel metal awning, a small low serving hatch, heavily weathered dull gray sheet metal, restrained rust seams, mossy lower stains, and rows of plain unlabeled amber beer bottles behind the glass.
content.desired_read: An instantly recognizable provincial Russian beer stall from the 1990s, rendered as a cute floating Machi Koro-style miniature.
recognition_details: narrow faceted kiosk silhouette with a raised boxy roof crown
small low serving hatch beneath a broad bowed two-panel sheet-metal awning
framed glass display bays wrapping the front and right side
old dull-gray cladding with chipped paint, oxidized edges, mossy stains, and restrained rust seams
rows of plain unlabeled amber beer bottles visible behind the glass
content.miniature_base: A compact irregular patch of cracked charcoal asphalt and chipped concrete with one sparse grass tuft, fully isolated on transparency.
simplify: the kiosk into a few chunky gray metal-frame and glass masses
wear, oxidation, moss, and rust into a handful of flat graphic patches rather than realistic texture
the beer display into orderly rows of simple repeated amber bottle silhouettes
omit: all letters, numbers, words, prices, menus, labels, signage, logos, graffiti, bottle labels, posters, and pseudo-writing
all signboards and menu boards, including blank ones
people, cars, streets, trees, surrounding buildings, fruit and vegetable displays, product advertising, and branded packaging
realistic textures, dramatic lighting, full scenery, and full-card composition
content.target_impression: The same whimsical illustrator who drew classic Machi Koro establishments has turned the supplied shabby gray park kiosk into a deadpan 1990s Russian beer stall.

anti_patterns: Do not generate a full card.
Do not generate any background, sky, clouds, header, footer, frame, coin, or category icon.
Do not create a realistic painting or architectural rendering.
Do not create a full streetscape or connect the scene to the bottom of the card.
Do not generate any letters, numbers, words, prices, menus, labels, signage, logos, graffiti, bottle labels, license-plate characters, or pseudo-text anywhere.
Do not include even a blank signboard or menu board.
Do not clip any part of the kiosk, awning, props, or miniature base.
final_prompt_summary: Edit the existing card illustration using the supplied kiosk photo as the reference for architecture, age, and weathering. Preserve the cute flat Machi Koro-style miniature language, compact right-facing three-quarter composition, clean outlines, simple graphic shading, isolated pavement base, full visibility, and transparent background. Transform the building into a narrow, slightly tall, old gray prefab kiosk with clipped corners, framed glass display bays wrapping the front and right side, a raised boxy roof crown, a broad bowed two-panel sheet-metal awning on thin supports, and a small low serving hatch. Make it noticeably shabby, old, gray, and rusty: dull weathered gray metal, broad chipped-paint patches, oxidized edges, mossy lower stains, and restrained reddish-brown rust seams, all stylized rather than photorealistic. Replace the former crate/bin emphasis with rows of simple identical plain amber and brown beer bottles and a few aluminum beer cans behind the glass, plus at most one small plain metal keg. Absolutely no letters, numbers, words, prices, menus, labels, signs, logos, graffiti, bottle labels, pseudo-glyphs, posters, banners, or signboards. Do not copy any text or produce from the reference photo. No people, vehicles, streets, trees, surrounding buildings, opaque backdrop, realistic texture noise, dramatic lighting, or clipped content.
